Summary: Marcionism taught in the 2nd century that the God of the Old Testament was different from and inferior to the God revealed by Jesus. Marcion rejected the Old Testament and edited the New Testament writings he accepted.
Beliefs: The Old Testament God is a separate and harsh creator; The God of Jesus is only love and mercy; The Old Testament should be rejected; Only parts of Luke and Paul's letters are Scripture
Controversy: Marcion was excommunicated in Rome AD 144; his teaching prompted the church to clarify the canon of Scripture
ChristianResponse: The church affirmed one God revealed in both Testaments and preserved the Old Testament as Scripture, citing Luke 24:27 and 2 Timothy 3:16.
RelatedDoctrines: Canon of Scripture; Nature of God; Old Testament
